Sensabaugh''' (born October 30, 2003) is an American [[college basketball]] player for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]] of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. ==Early life and high school career== Sensabaugh grew up in [[Orlando, Florida]] and attended [[Lake Highland Preparatory School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/all-central-florida-sports-teams/os-sp-hs-boys-basketball-brice-sensabaugh-winter-2022-all-area-central-florida-20220327-4bcyob6ptbdapen233bvi3kbze-story.html|title=Lake Highland Prep senior tops boys basketball All-Area|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=March 27, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} He was the team's leading scorer as a sophomore but missed his entire junior season due to a [[meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] injury.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-basketball-private-preview-1123-20211123-w42jxbkitncnbaqpy46iebzmre-story.html|title=Brice Sensabaugh back for Lake Highland|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=November 23, 2021|access-date=January 18, 2023}}{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/ohio-state/LongFormArticle/Ohio-State-Buckeyes-mens-basketball-incoming-freshman-Brice-Sensabaugh-to-contribute-at-forward-spots-188167867/|title=New Buckeyes: Sensabaugh bounced back from injury to win Mr. Basketball award|first=Steve|last=Helwagen|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=May 31, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} Sensabaugh averaged 25.1 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game as a senior and was named [[Florida Mr. Basketball]].{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-mr-basketball-0405-20220404-etfbevflufhl3o2jqnw57uxpua-story.html|title=Ohio State signee Brice Sensabaugh wins Florida Mr Basketball|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=April 4, 2022|access-date=January 17, 2023}} He was rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and committed to playing college basketball for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]].{{cite web|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/2021/09/28/ohio-state-buckeyes-basketball-recruiting-orlando-lake-highland-prep-brice-sensabaugh-commits/5893641001/|title=Brice Sensabaugh commits to Ohio State basketball, Chris Holtmann|work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=September 28, 2021|access-date=January 17, 2023}} After graduating from high school, Sensabaugh played in the [[pro–am]] Kingdom Summer League in Ohio and scored 51 points in a game.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/boys-basketball/os-sp-hs-basketball-report-0707-20220706-d6cvn62fyjap5jrkdr7llifw44-story.html|title=Brice Sensabaugh scores 51; Sean Stewart aids U.S. 17U (4-0)|work=[[Orlando Sentinel]]|date=July 6, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} ==College career== Sensabaugh entered his freshman season at Ohio State as a key reserve off of the bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/11/18/prolific-brice-sensabaugh-impressing-early-for-ohio-state-basketball/69657372007/|title=Prolific Brice Sensabaugh impressing early for Ohio State basketball|work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=November 18, 2022|access-date=January 18, 2023}} Sensabaugh was named the [[Big Ten Conference]] Freshman of the Week for three straight weeks.{{cite web|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/01/03/brice-sensabaughs-ridiculous-god-given-touch-leading-ohio-state/69770505007/|title=Brice Sensabaugh's 'ridiculous, God-given touch' leading Ohio State|work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=January 3, 2023|access-date=January 18, 2023}} He was named third team All-Big Ten and to the Big Ten All-Freshman team at the end of the regular season.{{cite web|url=https://www.dispatch.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2023/03/07/ohio-states-brice-sensabaugh-justice-sueing-all-big-ten-honors/69981237007/|title=Ohio State's Brice Sensabaugh, others earn all-Big Ten honors|work=[[The Columbus Dispatch]]|date=March 7, 2023|access-date=March 23, 2023}} After the season, Sensabaugh declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] while maintaining his eligibility.{{cite web|url=https://www.cleveland.com/osu/2023/03/what-brice-sensabaugh-declaring-for-the-nba-draft-means-for-ohio-state-basketball.html|title=What Brice Sensabaugh declaring for the NBA Draft means for Ohio State basketball|first=Stephen|last=Means|website=[[Cleveland.com]]|date=March 25, 2023|access-date=March 27, 2023}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
